findings.name: CPUID hypervisor-present bit
findings.description: CPUID leaf 1, ECX bit 31 -- set by every mainstream hypervisor to advertise itself to the guest.
findings.error_detail: CPUID unavailable (non-x86 host or native helper failed to build)

findings.name: CPUID hypervisor vendor string
findings.description: CPUID leaf 0x40000000 -- the hypervisor vendor ID string (e.g. 'KVMKVMKVM').
findings.error_detail: CPUID unavailable (non-x86 host or native helper failed to build)

findings.name: CPU brand string (Pafish-class)
findings.description: CPUID leaves 0x80000002-4 -- Pafish's classic check for 'QEMU Virtual CPU'/'Common KVM processor'/Hyper-V's 'Virtual CPU'.
findings.error_detail: CPUID unavailable (non-x86 host or native helper failed to build)

findings.name: PCI vendor ID enumeration
findings.description: Scans /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/vendor for known virtio/QEMU/VMware/VirtualBox/Xen PCI vendor IDs.

findings.name: Loaded guest-integration kernel modules
findings.description: Reads /proc/modules for virtio/VirtualBox/VMware/Xen/Hyper-V paravirtualised driver modules.
findings.remediation: Blacklist/unload paravirtualised guest driver modules on the golden image before freezing it.

findings.name: Guest-integration agent binaries on disk
findings.description: Checks for qemu-ga/VBoxService/vmtoolsd binaries, whose presence alone identifies a VM guest.

findings.name: SCSI device vendor string
findings.description: /proc/scsi/scsi Vendor: field -- Pafish's 'QEMU SCSI key' check, generalised to the /proc source.

findings.name: Block device vendor/model strings
findings.description: /sys/block/*/device/{vendor,model}, checked against known virtual-disk vendor strings.

findings.name: systemd-detect-virt
findings.description: Cross-checks against systemd's own virtualization detector -- an independent authoritative source that Pafish/al-khaser/VMAware (Windows-only) have no equivalent of.
findings.remediation: systemd itself identifies this as 'xen'; see the corresponding CPUID/DMI findings for the specific spoofing gap.

findings.name: Logical CPU count
findings.description: A sandbox is commonly provisioned with very few vCPUs (<= 2).

findings.name: Total RAM
findings.description: A sandbox is commonly provisioned with very little RAM (<= 4 GiB).

findings.name: Primary disk size
findings.description: A sandbox is commonly provisioned with a small disk (<= 60 GiB).

findings.name: Container/WSL execution environment
findings.description: Checks for /.dockerenv, cgroup container markers, and WSL's kernel version string.

findings.name: Cloud instance-metadata endpoint
findings.description: Attempts a short-timeout request to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ -- reachability alone identifies a cloud VM. Not checked by Pafish/al-khaser/VMAware, which predate cloud-native detonation infrastructure.

findings.name: Known analysis-framework marker paths
findings.description: Checks for Cuckoo/INetSim installation directories left on the host.
findings.remediation: These paths belong on the host/service VM, not inside the detonation guest -- remove them from the golden image.

findings.name: System uptime
findings.description: Low uptime suggests the VM was booted specifically for this analysis run (PAfish-class check).

findings.name: RDTSC-around-CPUID VM-exit timing
findings.description: Times the RDTSC delta across a CPUID call (which always forces a VM exit under KVM) and compares the median cost against a bare-metal-plausible threshold.
findings.error_detail: RDTSC/CPUID unavailable (non-x86 host or native helper failed to build)

findings.name: Shell history depth
findings.description: A near-empty ~/.bash_history/.zsh_history is implausible for a machine with real usage history.

findings.name: Filesystem 'wear and tear' age
findings.description: Counts files under $HOME older than a week; a home directory that is all brand-new is a tell.

findings.name: Installed package count
findings.description: A machine with very few installed packages beyond the base OS looks freshly provisioned.

findings.name: Installed font count
findings.description: A machine with fewer than 30 fonts installed looks like a minimal/headless provisioning rather than a real desktop.

findings.name: Running process count
findings.description: A machine running fewer than 40 processes looks like a minimal sandbox rather than a real desktop session.
findings.remediation: A minimal process list is expected right after boot; re-run this check after normal desktop session startup.

findings.name: Malware-analysis tooling running
findings.description: Checks the process list for debuggers/sniffers/disassemblers whose presence alone signals analysis.

findings.name: Hostname/username plausibility (substring)
findings.description: Hostnames/usernames like 'sandbox' or 'malware' are an easy, high-confidence tell malware checks for.

findings.name: Username exact-match blacklist (al-khaser style)
findings.description: al-khaser checks the current username against an exact-match blacklist (e.g. 'test', 'sandbox', 'john doe') rather than a substring -- short names like 'test' would false-positive under substring matching.

findings.name: NIC MAC address OUI
findings.description: Compares the first 3 octets of each NIC's MAC against well-known virtual-NIC vendor prefixes.
